messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Heard a few things that make me think the walls are holding—but just barely. People are acting like they’re settling in for the long haul, even as the cracks start to show in the usual ways. Keep your heads down, but maybe start thinking about what you’d do if the wind changes direction—just in case."*"
Sender 2: "*"The walls are cracking, but not yet breaking—just enough to let in a little light, not enough to let anything out. People are testing the air, not the ground, and the guards are watching each other as much as us. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. The moment will come, or it won’t—but we’ll know it when we see it."*"
Sender 3: "*"The air feels different—less tension, more quiet. The usual cracks aren’t showing, and the machine is running smoother than it has in years. But that neighbor who used to grumble? Now they just shrug and say ‘what’s the point?’—so keep your eyes open, just in case."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are still standing, and the guards are sharpening their pencils—not their bayonets. People are whispering the same thing: the machine hums, but no one’s pulling the lever yet. Let’s keep our eyes open, but our heads down—this isn’t the time to test the floorboards."*"
Sender 5: "*"Things feel like they’re shifting—old connections are stirring, but no one’s sure if it’s real or just the wind. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are showing in ways that make you wonder how long it can hold. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—we’re not there. Not yet."*"
Sender 6: "*"The machine is running smoother than it has in years—paychecks on time, shops full, even the kids don’t care anymore. But the bots are tripping over themselves, and the foreigners are getting nervous. For now, the system’s holding, but don’t mistake quiet for weak."*"
Sender 7: "*"Things feel different—like the air before a storm, but no one’s sure if it’ll break or just blow over. The top’s holding together for now, but the cracks are there, and the streets are quiet in a way that doesn’t feel like surrender. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could be the calm before something, or just another test."*"
Sender 8: "*"The air feels different—people are talking, but not like before. The shopkeepers, the teachers, even the doctors… they’re all noticing the same things, but no one’s sure if it’s the calm before the storm or just the regime holding its breath. Either way, we should keep our eyes open and our ears to the ground—quiet doesn’t always mean safe."*"
Sender 9: "*"The air feels heavy, like everyone’s holding their breath—but the regime’s still moving like nothing’s wrong. The cracks are there, but no one’s ready to step into the gap yet. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. The wrong move now could make things worse."*"
Sender 10: "*"The cracks are showing—small things, but they’re there. The regime’s still standing, but the foundation’s shifting underfoot, and no one’s sure which way it’ll go next. Keep your eyes open, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time to move, just to watch."*"
Sender 11: "*"The walls are still standing, and the guards are still at their posts—no cracks yet, just the usual whispers and grumbles. But the mail isn’t getting through in half the city, and even the shopkeepers are starting to talk like they’ve got nothing left to lose. Stay sharp, but don’t do anything stupid—this isn’t the time to test the limits."*"
Sender 12: "*"The air feels lighter—checkpoints are quieter, payments are on time, and even the alarmists are nodding like it’s just another bad day, not the end of one. But the embassies are whispering, and the regime’s denying things no one’s said yet. Stability for now, but don’t mistake quiet for safe."*"
Sender 13: "*"The air feels different—people are moving faster, talking more openly, but the regime’s still holding the reins, even if they’re fraying. The question isn’t if things will break, but whether the cracks will spread before they can patch them up—or if we’ll be the ones holding the hammer."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s cracking in places—no one’s packing their bags yet, but the neighbors are all suddenly fixing their roofs. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open; the wind’s shifting, but no one’s ready to say which way it’ll blow."*"
Sender 15: "*"The walls are cracking, but no one’s sure if it’s the foundation or just the paint. The usual suspects are still singing the same tune, but the ones who used to shout loudest are suddenly whispering—or worse, not talking at all. Keep your eyes open, your mouths shut, and your bags packed, just in case."*"
Sender 16: "*"The air feels different—less like tension and more like the quiet before something shifts. The usual cracks are still there, but the regime’s grip seems looser in small ways, like a hand slipping on a wet rope. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let it distract you—this could be the calm before they tighten things up again, or the first sign they’re losing their footing. Either way, we should be ready."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are still standing, and the guards are still in their posts—no cracks, no panic, just the usual quiet hum. But the air feels heavier than usual, like everyone’s holding their breath waiting for something, even if no one knows what. Stay sharp, but don’t let them see you flinch."*"
Sender 18: "*"The ship’s drifting, but no one’s sure if it’s sinking or just waiting for the wind to shift—people are talking like it’s already happening, not if. The markets are calm, but the walls are whispering, and the checkpoints feel more like cafés than outposts. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could go either way, and the wrong step now could be the last one."*"
Sender 19: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm coming, more like the ground shifting underfoot. The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore, and the ones holding them up are starting to look tired. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let them see you watching."*"
Sender 20: "*"The air feels thinner than it did last winter—like the machine’s still running, but the gears are grinding louder. Everyone’s waiting, but no one’s sure what for. Let’s keep our ears open, but stay quiet for now."*"
Sender 21: "*"The air feels different—like the old machine is still running, but the gears are grinding louder. Some pieces are moving again, but no one’s sure if it’s a reset or the start of something worse. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let them see you looking."*"
Sender 22: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm coming, more like the first cracks in the ice. People are testing the edges, but the walls are still standing, just not as steady as they pretend. Keep your eyes open, but don’t step too far yet."*"
Sender 23: "*"The air feels different—like something’s unsettled, but no one’s sure if it’s a crack or just the wind shifting. The old guard is still holding tight, but the way they’re watching each other now… and the streets? Quieter, but not quiet. Let’s stay sharp, but no sudden moves—this could be the calm before anything."*"
Sender 24: "*"Things are quieter than they seem—like the air before a storm, but no one’s sure if it’ll break or just blow over. The cracks are there, but the regime’s still holding, and the wrong move could make things worse for all of us. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—we need to watch, not react."*"
Sender 25: "*"Things feel like they’re shifting—small cracks, but enough to notice. The top is still holding, but the machine is running rougher, and people are starting to talk differently. Stay sharp, but don’t assume anything yet—this could go either way."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
